/-!
# Conjecture 4.5

by S. I. Adian

b) Is it true that an arbitrary finitely presented group has either polynomial or
exponential growth?

In other words, is there no finitely presented group of intermediate growth? Only part b)
of Problem 4.5 is stated here; part a), the same question for finitely generated groups,
was answered in the negative by Grigorchuk.

A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to the quotient of a free group of finite
rank by the normal closure of a finite set of relators. The growth of a finitely generated
group $G$ is measured by the growth function $\gamma_S(n)$ of a finite generating set $S$,
which counts the elements of $G$ that are products of at most $n$ elements of
$S \cup S^{-1}$. The group has polynomial growth if $\gamma_S(n) \le C n^d$ for all $n > 0$
and some constants $C > 0$, $d \in \mathbb{N}$ (`GromovPolynomialGrowth.HasPolynomialGrowth`),
and exponential growth if $\gamma_S(n) \ge c^n$ for all $n$ and some constant $c > 1$
(equivalently, since $\gamma_S$ is submultiplicative, the growth rate
$\lim_n \gamma_S(n)^{1/n}$ is strictly greater than $1$). Neither notion depends on the
choice of the finite generating set $S$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and some finite set $R$
of relators, that is, to the quotient of the free group on $n$ generators by the normal
closure of $R$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Group.FG` (too weak: finitely generated only); `PresentedGroup` (a construction, not a predicate on an abstract group); no `Module.FinitePresentation`-style analogue for groups exists.
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.5».IsFinitelyPresented
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has `Group.FG` (finitely generated) and `PresentedGroup rels`, but no predicate saying a group admits a finite presentation. Defined as ∃ n, ∃ finite rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)), Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G), exactly as the decomposition notes prescribe. Two `category test` lemmas (any `PresentedGroup` with finite relators; `FreeGroup (Fin n)`) are proved.

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and some finite set $R$
of relators, that is, to the quotient of the free group on $n$ generators by the normal
closure of $R$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

justification.closest_existing_considered: `GromovPolynomialGrowth.HasSuperPolynomialGrowth` (strictly weaker: intermediate-growth groups satisfy it, so using it would trivialize the question); Mathlib's `ExpGrowth.expGrowthInf/expGrowthSup` on ℝ≥0∞ sequences (would work but adds an unnecessary ENNReal layer; the elementary form is closer to the notebook's usage).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.5».HasExponentialGrowth
justification.why_needed: The repo provides `HasPolynomialGrowth` and `HasSuperPolynomialGrowth` but nothing for exponential growth. Defined as ∃ finite generating S, ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n, c ^ n ≤ GrowthFunction S n, mirroring the shape of `HasPolynomialGrowth`. This is equivalent to the standard 'growth rate lim γ_S(n)^{1/n} > 1' (by Fekete's lemma the limit equals inf_n γ_S(n)^{1/n} for the submultiplicative γ_S, so one may take c = the growth rate; conversely c ≤ the rate), and is independent of the finite generating set. API/test lemmas proved: exponential growth implies `Group.FG`; finite groups do not have exponential growth.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  haveI : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨_, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question (so `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G, FinitelyPresented G → HasPolynomialGrowth G ∨ HasExponentialGrowth G`), i.e. no finitely presented group has intermediate growth; implicit conventions: 'finitely presented' (not in Mathlib) means G ≅ FreeGroup (Fin n) modulo the normal closure of a finite set of relators, growth is measured via the word-ball counting function of a finite generating set (repo helper GromovPolynomialGrowth.GrowthFunction/HasPolynomialGrowth) and its polynomial/exponential type is independent of the chosen finite generating set, 'exponential growth' means the growth function is bounded below by c^n for some c > 1 (equivalently the growth rate lim γ(n)^{1/n} exceeds 1), and part a) (the same question for finitely generated groups, settled negatively by Grigorchuk) is not part of the statement and must not be added.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematics: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G → HasPolynomialGrowth G ∨ HasExponentialGrowth G`, with finite presentation as `G ≃* PresentedGroup rels` for a finite `rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))` (Mathlib's `PresentedGroup` is literally the quotient by the normal closure) and exponential growth as `∃ finite generating S, ∃ c > 1, ∀ n, c^n ≤ GrowthFunction S n`. I verified this against the standard notions: by Fekete's lemma for the submultiplicative γ_S the 'for all n' bound with some c > 1 is equivalent to growth rate lim γ_S(n)^{1/n} > 1 (n = 0 gives 1 ≤ 1); both growth types are independent of the finite generating set so the existential over S (matching the repo's `HasPolynomialGrowth`) is faithful; inclusive ∨ is harmless since the two types are mutually exclusive; quantifying over `Type` loses nothing since finitely presented groups are countable and all predicates are isomorphism-invariant; `answer(True)` = positive answer, `answer(False)` = negative. c04 was chosen as the base because it follows the repo naming convention `kourovka.«4.5».parts.b` (c01/c02 use `parts.b`, which deviates from the `kourovka.«N»` convention and the slot id) and has the most complete API/test coverage for the bespoke definitions, as CONTRIBUTING.md requests. I added c05's `IsFinitelyPresented.fg` API lemma and trimmed the docstrings. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning on the main theorem.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.5

by S. I. Adian

b) Is it true that an arbitrary finitely presented group has either polynomial or
exponential growth?

In other words, is there no finitely presented group of intermediate growth? Only part b)
of Problem 4.5 is stated here; part a), the same question for finitely generated groups,
was answered in the negative by Grigorchuk.

A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to the quotient of a free group of finite
rank by the normal closure of a finite set of relators. The growth of a finitely generated
group $G$ is measured by the growth function $\gamma_S(n)$ of a finite generating set $S$,
which counts the elements of $G$ that are products of at most $n$ elements of
$S \cup S^{-1}$. The group has polynomial growth if $\gamma_S(n) \le C n^d$ for all $n > 0$
and some constants $C > 0$, $d \in \mathbb{N}$ (`GromovPolynomialGrowth.HasPolynomialGrowth`),
and exponential growth if $\gamma_S(n) \ge c^n$ for all $n$ and some constant $c > 1$
(equivalently, since $\gamma_S$ is submultiplicative, the growth rate
$\lim_n \gamma_S(n)^{1/n}$ is strictly greater than $1$). Neither notion depends on the
choice of the finite generating set $S$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.5»

open GromovPolynomialGrowth

/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and some finite set $R$
of relators, that is, to the quotient of the free group on $n$ generators by the normal
closure of $R$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

/-- A group has exponential growth if there is a finite generating set $S$ whose growth
function $\gamma_S$ is bounded below by a geometric sequence $c^n$ with $c > 1$. Equivalently,
the growth rate $\lim_n \gamma_S(n)^{1/n}$ is strictly greater than $1$. -/
def HasExponentialGrowth (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (S : Set G), S.Finite ∧ Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, c ^ n ≤ (GrowthFunction S n : ℝ)

/-- A group presented by finitely many generators and finitely many relators is finitely
presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} {rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))}
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨n, rels, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- The free group on finitely many generators is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup (n : ℕ) : IsFinitelyPresented (FreeGroup (Fin n)) :=
  ⟨n, ∅, Set.finite_empty, ⟨(QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq
    (le_bot_iff.mp (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (Set.empty_subset _)))).trans
    (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := FreeGroup (Fin n)))⟩⟩

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  haveI : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨_, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

/-- A group of exponential growth is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem HasExponentialGrowth.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : HasExponentialGrowth G) :
    Group.FG G :=
  ⟨⟨h.choose_spec.1.toFinset, by simpa using h.choose_spec.2.1⟩⟩

/-- A finite group does not have exponential growth. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_hasExponentialGrowth_of_finite {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] :
    ¬ HasExponentialGrowth G := by
  rintro ⟨S, -, -, c, hc, h⟩
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := pow_unbounded_of_one_lt (Nat.card G : ℝ) hc
  refine absurd ((h n).trans ?_) (not_le.mpr hn)
  exact_mod_cast Set.ncard_le_card _

/--
b) Is it true that an arbitrary finitely presented group has either polynomial or
exponential growth?

That is, does every finitely presented group $G$ have a finite generating set $S$ whose
growth function $\gamma_S$ is either bounded above by a polynomial $C n^d$ (for $n > 0$) or
bounded below by $c^n$ for some $c > 1$? Equivalently, is there no finitely presented group
of intermediate growth?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.5».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G →
      HasPolynomialGrowth G ∨ HasExponentialGrowth G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.5»

items: Groups are quantified over `Type` (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean); every finitely presented group is countable, so this loses no generality up to isomorphism, and `IsFinitelyPresented` is isomorphism-invariant by construction.

`HasExponentialGrowth` requires the lower bound `c ^ n ≤ γ_S(n)` for all `n` rather than eventually; the two forms are equivalent (for the ∀ n version take c equal to the growth rate ω = inf γ_S(n)^{1/n} > 1), and n = 0 is harmless since γ_S(0) = 1.

Both growth predicates are of the form '∃ finite generating set S such that …' (following the repo's `HasPolynomialGrowth`); polynomial/exponential type is independent of the chosen finite generating set, so this matches the informal notion.

The bespoke definitions are placed in the problem file (the task permits only one output file); a reviewer may prefer moving `IsFinitelyPresented` and `HasExponentialGrowth` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as reusable definitions.
Part a) of Problem 4.5 (finitely generated groups, refuted by Grigorchuk) is mentioned only as context in the module docstring and is deliberately not formalized, per the decomposition table.

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised and I found none. The statement (v46 text) contains only part b); part a) (finitely generated groups, refuted by Grigorchuk) is mentioned only as context in the module docstring and is not formalized. Bespoke definitions `IsFinitelyPresented` and `HasExponentialGrowth` live in the problem file (namespace `Kourovka.«4.5»`); a maintainer may prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as they are reusable. Minor residual modeling choice: exponential growth is stated with the lower bound for all n rather than 'eventually' or 'up to a constant factor'; these are equivalent for growth functions of finite generating sets (submultiplicativity), so no faithfulness loss.
